newsitem.title: USA: Senate panel gives immunity to potential witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Senate panel gives immunity to potential witnesses.

text.p: The Senate Governmental Affairs Committee voted 16-0 on Friday to grant immunity to four potential witnesses in its investigation of campaign finance practices.

Chairman Fred Thompson, Tennessee Republican, and Ohio Sen. John Glenn, the Democratic leader on the committee, said the vote indicated bipartisan agreement for the opening of committee hearings on July 8.
"We are getting our sea legs," Thompson said. Glenn said that despite some disagreements the committee had a "golden opportunity" to lay the foundation for campaign finance reform.

Committee members agreed to decide by July 7 on a list of 34 potential subpoenas to a wide range of organisations for information about "soft money" donations to political parties. Groups like the environmentalist Sierra Club and the conservative Heritage Foundation were on the list.

Immunity was granted to Hueitsan Huang and Siuw Moi Lian, two Buddist monks at a West Coast temple where Vice President Al Gore spoke at a fundraising event. Immunity was also granted to Xi Ping Wang and Yue F. Chu, associates of Democratic fundraiser Charlie Trie.
